rule: Within task-SDK coordinator modules, use `exc_info=True` as a structlog keyword argument instead of `error=str(exc)` when logging caught exceptions at debug/warning level, so the traceback is preserved for debuggability.
trigger: log.debug(..., error=str(exc)) or log.warning(..., error=str(exc)) inside task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/
rationale: exc_info is a special structlog key that attaches the full traceback; converting the exception to a string loses it and makes post-mortem debugging harder.

evidence.excerpt: exc_info=True would keep the traceback for debuggability

rule: Do not define a separate `__version__` attribute inside `airflow.sdk.coordinators.*` sub-packages; the canonical distribution version is exposed only at `airflow.sdk.__version__`.
trigger: diff adds `__version__ = "..."` or `"__version__"` in `__all__` inside task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/coordinators/*/
rationale: Keeping a separate subpackage version risks confusion and stale or incorrect version reporting compared with the single Task SDK distribution version.

evidence.excerpt: inconsistent with the rest of the Task SDK; risks confusion and stale version reporting

rule: Import `NotRequired` (and other symbols added in later Python minor versions) with a `try/except ImportError` stdlib-first fallback before importing from `typing_extensions`, to support the full Python version range Airflow targets.
trigger: diff adds a bare `from typing_extensions import NotRequired` (or similar backport) without a stdlib try/except guard
rationale: Airflow supports multiple Python versions; unconditionally importing from typing_extensions bypasses the stdlib when available and is inconsistent with the project's compatibility pattern.

evidence.excerpt: try: from typing import NotRequired except ImportError: from typing_extensions

rule: Function-local imports are only permitted when a circular import makes a module-level import impossible; otherwise move all imports to module scope.
trigger: diff adds an import statement inside a function body where the same module is already imported at the top of the file or no circular-import comment explains the deferral
rationale: Keeping imports at module scope avoids repeated imports, follows the project's import-style rules, and makes dependency relationships explicit.

evidence.excerpt: move to module scope; project's import-style rules unless circular-import reason

rule: Task-SDK mapper classes exported in the public API must fully implement all abstract methods of their base class (including `to_upstream()`); incomplete implementations must be kept abstract or unexported until finished.
trigger: diff adds a concrete mapper class in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/partition_mappers/ that inherits RollupMapper without overriding to_upstream()
rationale: Exporting a class as usable when calls to an inherited method raise NotImplementedError misleads users and diverges from the airflow-core reference implementation.

rule: When a Task-SDK API method (e.g. `Variable.keys()`) only queries the metadata database and does not consult secrets backends, the docstring must include an explicit `.. note::` block documenting the asymmetry with `Variable.get()` and why secrets backends are excluded.
trigger: diff adds a Variable.keys() or similar listing method in task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/definitions/variable.py without a note about secrets-backend exclusion
rationale: Users running AwsSecretsManagerBackend or other backends will reasonably expect listing APIs to match the lookup behaviour of Variable.get(); the omission must be intentional and documented.

evidence.excerpt: add a note calling out that asymmetry is a deliberate design decision

rule: Exception classes defined in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/exceptions.py` that are only raised (and not caught) within the Task SDK must not be imported into `airflow-core`, even in tests; tests for those exceptions must reside in the SDK test tree.
trigger: diff imports an exception from airflow.sdk.exceptions inside airflow-core source or airflow-core/tests/
rationale: Importing SDK exceptions into core creates an unwanted cross-boundary dependency; tests belong in the same component that owns the code under test.

rule: The `supervise_callback` function must call `_make_process_nondumpable()` before spawning a subprocess, exactly as `supervise_task` does, to prevent core dumps from leaking secrets present in callback credentials (Notifier tokens, connection passwords, etc.).
trigger: diff adds or modifies a supervise_callback function in callback_supervisor.py without a call to _make_process_nondumpable()
rationale: Callbacks handle connection credentials such as Slack tokens and PagerDuty keys; omitting _make_process_nondumpable() creates a secret-leakage risk via core dumps that supervise_task already guards against.

rule: When invoking a callback callable with context kwargs, only pass `context` when `accepts_context` returns True AND the context value is not None; never forward `context=None` to a callback.
trigger: diff passes **callback_kwargs unconditionally to callback_callable when accepts_context() is True, without checking context is not None
rationale: Callbacks that previously received no context argument would now receive context=None, breaking the old semantics and potentially crashing callbacks that do not expect a None context.

rule: Exception log calls inside `callback_supervisor.py` must include structured identifying fields (`callback_id=`, `pid=`) to distinguish concurrent callback failures in logs, mirroring the `ActivitySubprocess` pattern in `supervisor.py`.
trigger: diff adds log.exception(...) or log.error(...) in callback_supervisor.py without callback_id or pid keyword arguments
rationale: When multiple callbacks run concurrently a bare message is insufficient to correlate the log line with the failing callback; the ActivitySubprocess equivalent already sets this pattern.

rule: All datetime fields placed into a callback context dict must be wrapped with `coerce_datetime` (from `airflow.sdk._shared.timezones`) to produce `pendulum.DateTime` objects, consistent with `RuntimeTaskInstance.get_template_context()` and the triggerer-side context builder.
trigger: diff populates a context dict in callback_supervisor.py with datetime fields from DagRunResult or similar without calling coerce_datetime()
rationale: Callbacks on the executor path would return stdlib datetime objects while triggerer/task callbacks return pendulum; user code calling .in_timezone() or .add(days=1) works on one path and crashes on the other.

evidence.excerpt: executor-path callbacks get stdlib datetimes; triggerer-path get pendulum; inconsistent

rule: When renaming message types in `comms.py`, update the message-type sync test allowlists in `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_processor.py` and `airflow-core/tests/unit/jobs/test_triggerer_job.py` in the same PR.

rationale: Both test files build the live type set from get_args(ToTask)/get_args(ToSupervisor) and diff it against hardcoded allowlists; a rename causes the new names to fall into task_diff/supervisor_diff and the assert-not-diff checks fail.

rule: Partition keys accumulated for the same task instance must be stored as a set (deduplicated), not a list, consistent with how asset aliases handle repeated keys.
trigger: diff uses a list field (e.g. attrs.field(factory=list)) for partition_keys on a task-instance context object and appends without deduplication
rationale: Asset aliases already use a set for keys to avoid duplicates within the same TI; partition_keys must follow the same pattern to avoid double-counting.

rule: In Asset lookup code, treat `Asset(uri=...)` as having `name == uri` (matching the DB storage convention), and do not treat `name=None` as a meaningful distinct state from `name=uri`.

rationale: Asset(uri='x') is stored in the DB as (uri='x', name='x'); SDK code that leaves name=None diverges from the persistence model and causes lookup mismatches.
